findings.problem: unwrap() on file I/O panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or not valid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return a typed error type (e.g. Result<Vec<Record>, Error>) and propagate with ? or map_err to distinguish Io, Utf8, and related failures

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing into a dynamically-sized Vec created from split(',') on arbitrary input
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero commas (no delimiter) produces a single-element Vec; indexing parts[0] succeeds but parts[1] at line 19 panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on Option<(&str, &str)> to exhaustively handle the zero-delimiter case, returning a typed Invalid error

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing into a dynamically-sized Vec created from split(',') on arbitrary input
findings.failure_mode: Any line with fewer than two comma-separated fields (empty lines, header rows, whitespace-only lines) causes a bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the Option; destructure to (_name, value_str) and parse only value_str

findings.problem: unwrap() on numeric parse panics on any non-numeric or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: A field containing 'abc', '3.14', or an empty string aborts the process instead of returning a typed Parse error
findings.fix: Use map_err to convert ParseIntError into a typed Error::Parse or Error::Invalid variant

findings.problem: Lossy narrowing cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid integer like 70000 parses successfully as u32 then truncates to 54416, silently corrupting data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u32::try_into().map_err(|_| Error::Overflow) to convert to u16 with explicit range checking

findings.problem: I/O (stdout write) embedded inside domain parsing logic that should be pure and deterministic
findings.failure_mode: Core logic has a side effect that makes it non-deterministic across environments (stdout redirected, TTY absent), mixes imperative shell concerns into the functional core, and produces observable output that varies by environment
findings.fix: Remove println! from load_frames; if logging is needed, pass a logging callback or return a metadata field in the typed error result

findings.problem: Record stores a raw String for name with no validation, encoding, or domain semantics enforced by the type system
findings.failure_mode: Any code constructing Record with an empty, whitespace-only, or otherwise invalid name is accepted by the compiler; illegal name state is representable
findings.fix: Introduce a Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty content, or at minimum make name private and add a constructor that enforces invariants

findings.problem: Function accepts arbitrary file content with no domain cap before allocation; the returned Vec grows without bound
findings.failure_mode: An attacker or misconfigured system can supply a massive file, causing unbounded memory allocation and potential OOM kill
findings.fix: Add a domain cap constant, validate line count against it before allocation, use try_reserve with checked capacity arithmetic, and return a typed Allocation error on failure

findings.problem: No typed error type exists in the crate; function signature returns a bare Vec with no error channel for the many fallible operations it performs
findings.failure_mode: Every failure mode (I/O, parse, bounds, overflow, allocation) is handled via panic rather than returning structured, recoverable errors
findings.fix: Define an enum Error { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid(String), Parse, Overflow, Allocation } and change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into owned Strings via intermediate Vec allocation when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Wastes heap allocation per line and creates String copies that could be &'str slices; the grammar expects exactly one comma so split_once is the idiomatic pattern
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') and match on Option<(&str, &str)> to extract (_name, value_str) as borrowed &str without any intermediate Vec or String allocation

residual_risk: This is a static-only review with no commands run (cargo check, clippy, cargo test were not executed per review constraints). All findings are drawn from source inspection against the absolute laws of the Holzman Rust candidate v9 skill. The crate as written violates 10 distinct rules including panic surfaces (unwrap on I/O and parse), unchecked indexing, lossy cast, hidden I/O in core logic, unbounded allocation, raw primitive domain state, and absent error taxonomy. Every finding is repairable without behavioral change to the happy path; all fixes convert panics to typed errors, eliminate intermediate allocations, remove side effects from pure logic, and add domain bounds. Full verification (cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets --all-features, cargo clippy, cargo test) is required after repair to confirm zero regressions and strict lint compliance.
